In this chapter, the focus is on reviewing basic electrophysiologic concepts that are important for clinicians. These include the structure and function of cardiac ion channels, their role in generating action potentials, the mechanisms of arrhythmias, and inherited and acquired channelopathies.
Ion channels are integral proteins in heart cells that regulate ion traffic, which in turn controls cardiac electrical activity. They generate the action potential, which is essential for automaticity, impulse conduction, excitation-contraction coupling, triggered automaticity, and arrhythmogenesis.
Key structures of ion channels in the heart include inwardly rectifying potassium (Kir) channels, which have 2 transmembrane segments and form functional channels when 4 subunits coassemble. These channels are often gated by ligands binding to channel protein subunits.
The learning objectives of this chapter are to review these basic electrophysiologic concepts and their relevance to clinical practice.
